description:
We’re going full-on retro today with a childhood classic: Malted Vanilla Ice Cream with Whoppers/Maltesers! 🍦✨
Remember sneaking a box of Whoppers (or Maltesers if you’re across the pond) at the movies? Now imagine that chocolatey, malty crunch swirled through creamy homemade vanilla ice cream… pure nostalgia in a bowl. 🎬🍫

This recipe is easy, fun, and packed with that classic malt shop vibe. Think 1950s diner milkshake — but colder, crunchier, and even more addictive. Grab your scoop and let’s churn up some sweet memories!

⸻

⏱ Timestamps:
00:00 – Intro & whats the difference between Whoppers and Maltesers?
01:35 – What you’ll need (ingredients)
02:26 – Malt Powder tip
03:38 – Custard or Stabilizer?
05:28 – Churning and suprise staciatella!
06:28 – Taste test
07:08 - Outro 

⸻

🔑 Keywords:
malted vanilla ice cream recipe, Whoppers ice cream, Maltesers ice cream, retro dessert recipe, nostalgic ice cream, homemade ice cream, malt shop ice cream, classic candy dessert, vintage dessert vibes, fun ice cream recipes, throwback dessert

comments.text:
Is there a general chat forum for YouTube members to ask you questions, and chat amoung ourselves? I watch a lot of your content, some from years back. It's hard to remember which video i asked a question on to check to an answer, not sure how far back you go to answer questions, and i don't think we get any notification if you do responded.
I'm setting myself a challenge to try to go as healthy as possible, to go organic, non-gmo and nutritious as possible, without being fanatical. After all, we're talking ice cream here.
 For function and health reasons, allulose seems to be almost revolutionary in dealing with sugar and orher sweetener issues.
I'm replacing all sugar with it, unless you give specific reasons otherwise. I'm fine tuning brown sugar with allulose/molasses. Tried an organic/non-gmo version of molasses that turned out to be blackstrap, only reveled in the small print. Going to try it with with a non-bkackstrap to see how different it is. 
Regarding dextrose,  is there a way allulose, or something similar, can replace?
Corn syrup has also been challenging for me. The concerns wth corn syrup tend to be high genetic modification, problematic chemicals being used, and high fructose added. Organic and non-gmo generally take care of the first issues, and many products are labled no high fructose. So far, the only product I've found that meets these goals adds other undesirable crap. The other issue is that most corn syrups add vanilla. I'd prefer adding the flavors myself per recipe. Fortunately, corn syrup seems to be added in very small quantities. 
You've mentioned using Golden Syrup as a replacement. I've seen recipes for do-it-yourself Golden Syrup, using using sugar and citric acid or lemon juice, and a fairly specific and long process that truns out some good stuff. Was wondering if allulose could be substituted, not just for the  flavor, but for the corn syrup effect. The problem might be that allulose is already a simple sugar, while regular sugar, and corn syrup can be broken down into glucose and fructose. Would inverting allulose, or making it a simple syrup, which i think is the same thing, work as a corn syrup replacement.
This is getting really long, but one last question. So far, the focus has been on mitigating the "bad" stuff. Time for some good, in addition to the incredible creamy goodness of your ice creams. Thinking protein.  You're already covered off the shelf protein powders. Problem with them is all the other stuff they add in. I looked into protein powders. Found some good ones using grass fed, organic, non-gmo (healthier) whey protein isolate. Isolate gets ride of the lactose and milk fat, which i would think would make formulations easier. They can also be gotten unflavored, making it more universal. Was thinking it might be a healthier option to nonfat milk powder. 
Would like your thoughts on all these things, maybe even doing vids on them, maybe adding allulose to you sugar series.
Hope you see this, and hope i see your response.
